```{r setup}
library(dataprep)
```

## Overview

`dataprep` 0.1.6 ships two reshaping backends, `melt()` and
`dcast()`, benchmarked here against **all seven major alternatives**
in the R and Python ecosystems:

* **R**: `reshape2`, `data.table`, `tidyr`
* **Python**: `pandas`, `polars`, `dask`, `duckdb`

Every cell is measured with `microbenchmark` using an adaptive
`times` rule: 100 iterations when the first call is under 10 ms,
down to a single iteration when it exceeds 10 s. Two statistics are
reported:

* **median** — the number to quote. Robust to scheduler and GC
  jitter.
* **mean** — the tail. A large mean / median ratio indicates
  one-off OS work or cache effects.

For every cell the tables also report the speed-up of `dataprep`
relative to **each** competitor, so the reader can see the full
gradient from "about the same" to "three orders of magnitude".

## Test environment

All timings in this document were measured on a single host:

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| CPU | 2× AMD EPYC 9965 (Turin, Zen 5c) |
| Physical cores | 384 (2 × 192) |
| Logical cores | 768 (SMT-2) |
| L1d | 18 MiB |
| L2 | 384 MiB |
| L3 | 768 MiB |
| NUMA nodes | 2 |
| RAM | 1.0 TiB DDR5 |
| Max frequency | 3.70 GHz |
| AVX-512 | Full (f, dq, ifma, cd, bw, vl, vbmi, vbmi2, vnni, bitalg, vpopcntdq, bf16) |
| OS | Ubuntu 25.10 |
| R | 4.5.1 |
| `dataprep` | 0.1.6 |
| `data.table` | 1.18.4 |
| `reshape2` | 1.4.5 |
| `tidyr` | 1.3.2 |
| Python | 3.13 |
| `pandas` | 3.0.3 |
| `polars` | 1.40.0 |
| `dask` | 2026.1.2 |
| `duckdb` | 1.5.5 |

### How to read these numbers

The host is a **dual-socket Zen 5c server with 768 logical cores,
768 MiB of L3 cache, and 1 TiB of RAM**. Two properties of this
environment shape the numbers that follow:

1. **The L3 cache is unusually large.** Most of the 1e6- and
   1e7-row cells fit entirely in L3. For `dataprep`, whose `melt`
   and `dcast` backends are memory-bandwidth bound, this
   translates into near-cache-speed medians. On a laptop with a
   32 MiB L3, the same operations still win, but the absolute
   times will be 3–10× larger.

2. **768 logical cores amplify the difference between native and
   interpreted dispatch.** `dataprep` uses OpenMP directly with a
   small fixed thread pool. `dask` and `duckdb` pay a per-task
   scheduling cost that grows with core count; on a 768-core host
   this overhead dominates their runtimes on small inputs.

Both effects *favour* `dataprep` in the numbers below. The
**relative ranking** is robust (it has been reproduced on 8- and
16-core machines), but the **absolute multipliers** — especially
the 2664× and 863× figures — should be interpreted as "best-case
on a very large machine". On a typical workstation the same
comparisons are within 10–100×.

## Cleaning pipeline

The 0.1.6 release rewrites every heavy cleaning routine in C++. The
table below compares against 0.1.5 on three dataset sizes from the
same source (SMEAR I Varrio forest). All numbers are medians in
milliseconds.

| Function | 500 rows | 7,640 rows | 49,422 rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `varidele` | 1.2× | 1.2× | 1.3× |
| `obsedele` | 19× | 102× | **560×** |
| `condextr` | 27× | 8× | 13.5× |
| `optisolu` | 47× | 26× | 29× |
| `dataprep` | 59× | 6.8× | 7.4× |

> **Note on `optisolu` cores.** The 0.1.5 implementation could
> crash when `cores > 16`, because its `parallel::makeCluster()`
> path gave each worker a full copy of the data. The benchmark
> above used `cores = 16` for both versions to keep the comparison
> fair. 0.1.6 shares read-only data across workers and accepts
> `cores = 64` safely, so the practical speed-up on a many-core
> host is **larger**.

| n_id | dataprep | reshape2 | data.table | tidyr | pandas | polars | dask | duckdb |

The `100 id` cell is the **only** case in the entire benchmark

`dataprep`.

## Cross-engine consistency

Both `melt()` and `dcast()` produce output **byte-identical to
`reshape2`** on every tested cell. All pairs of engines agree
pairwise within `tol = 1e-12`.

### `melt` consistency

| rows | n_id | n_val | engines passed | pairwise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 1 | 9 | 8/8 | all consistent |
| 100,000 | 1 | 9 | 8/8 | all consistent |
| 1,000 | 1 | 100 | 8/8 | all consistent |
| 10,000 | 10 | 10 | 8/8 | all consistent |

### `dcast` consistency

| n_long | n_id | n_levels | engines passed | pairwise |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | 2 | 5 | 8/8 | all consistent |
| 50,000 | 1 | 50 | 8/8 | all consistent |
| 50,000 | 10 | 10 | 8/8 | all consistent |
| 1,000,000 | 1 | 10 | 8/8 | all consistent |

Engines compared: `dataprep`, `reshape2`, `data.table`, `tidyr`,
`pandas`, `polars`, `dask`, `duckdb`.

## Summary

* **`melt()`** is the fastest engine across every tested cell. The
  speed-up spans **1.03×** (against `data.table` at 1e5 rows with
  one id column) to **2664×** (against `dask` on a 10000-column
  wide table). The **median across all melt cells and all
  competitors is above 30×**.
* **`dcast()`** is the fastest engine across every tested cell.
  The speed-up spans **3.7×** (against `polars` at 100 id columns)
  to **863×** (against `data.table` at 1e6 rows and 100 levels).
* **`melt()` and `dcast()` are byte-identical to `reshape2`** on
  every tested shape, within `1e-12`.

## Reproducing the benchmarks

The full runner is shipped under `inst/`:

* `benchmark_helpers.R` — adaptive per-tool runner with a 15 s
  first-call cap
* `melt_benchmark.R` — melt benchmark driver
* `dcast_benchmark.R` — dcast benchmark driver
* `melt_consistency.R` — 8-engine consistency check
* `dcast_consistency.R` — 8-engine consistency check

Scripts are disabled by default so that `R CMD check` does not run
them. To enable:

```{r eval=FALSE}
Sys.setenv(DATAPREP_RUN_BENCHMARK = "1")
source(system.file("melt_benchmark.R",  package = "dataprep"))
source(system.file("dcast_benchmark.R", package = "dataprep"))
```
